name: Dev pipeline
description: Coder writes the code, Reviewer approves it or sends it back with feedback (a loop bounded by max_loop_visits), a human approves the ship, Deployer opens a merge request in the project repository, or updates the one the run names by pushing the work onto its branch, and publishes a release when the run has no project.

nodes.message: Ship this change (release {{or .input.version "1.0.0"}} or a merge request)? Coder: {{.state.coder.summary}} Reviewer: {{.state.reviewer.feedback}}

nodes.task:
Ship the reviewed work. Coder's summary: {{.state.coder.summary}}. Files: {{range .state.coder.files}}{{.}} {{end}}. Reviewer: {{.state.reviewer.feedback}}

If your task's protocol block describes a project repository, open or update a merge request with the open_merge_request tool: title from the task ({{.input.task}}), description with the coder's summary and how it was tested. Finish with status "merge_request_opened" when it opened a new request and "merge_request_updated" when it pushed onto the request this run updates, and the merge_request_url the tool returned.
Otherwise publish the work in runs/$RUN_ID/ as release version {{or .input.version "1.0.0"}} with the deploy_release tool, including the files listed, with the summary as release notes, and finish with the release id and version the tool returned and a status of "deployed".
If the tool result says the action was rejected or is pending approval, finish with that status and no release id or URL.
